questions.question_text: Subsidiary books are:
options: Books in which similar transactions are recorded separately, e.g., purchases book and sales book
questions.explanation: They are subdivisions of the journal.

questions.question_text: Subsidiary books are maintained to:
options: Save time and labour by recording similar transactions together
questions.explanation: The journal would be too bulky otherwise.

questions.question_text: An advantage of subsidiary books is:
options: Division of work and saving of time and labour

questions.question_text: Which is a subsidiary book?
questions.explanation: Others: sales book, returns books, bills books, cash book.

questions.question_text: Journal proper records:
options: Transactions that do not fit in any subsidiary book, e.g., opening, closing, adjusting and rectification entries

questions.question_text: The purchases book records:
options: Credit purchases of goods meant for resale
questions.explanation: Only goods in which the firm deals.

questions.question_text: The sales book records:
The purchases returns book records:
The sales returns book records:
Cash purchases are not entered in the purchases book because:
options: They are recorded in the cash book
questions.explanation: The purchases book is only for credit purchases.

questions.question_text: Credit purchase of furniture is recorded in:
questions.explanation: Furniture is not goods for resale.

questions.question_text: Credit sale of an old asset is recorded in:
questions.explanation: The sales book is only for goods.

questions.question_text: A debit note is used in:
options: Purchases returns book (issued by the buyer)

questions.question_text: A credit note is used in:
options: Sales returns book (issued by the seller)

questions.question_text: In the purchases book, trade discount is:
options: Deducted from the list price and only the net amount recorded

questions.question_text: The total of the purchases book is posted to:
The total of the sales book is posted to:
The purchases returns total is posted to the _____ of Purchases Returns A/c, and the sales returns total to the _____ of Sales Returns A/c:
Under GST, the purchases and sales books show:
options: Separate columns for CGST/SGST/IGST in addition to the net amount
questions.explanation: Input tax is claimed on purchases.

questions.question_text: Purchases book: Ram 100 units @ Rs 300 less 10%; Mohan 50 units @ Rs 400; Sohan 80 units @ Rs 250 less 5%. Ram's net amount is:
The total of the purchases book in Q20 (27,000 + 20,000 + 19,000) is:
questions.explanation: Posted to the debit of Purchases A/c.

The total of the sales book in Q22 is:
Purchases returns: Ram 10 units @ Rs 270; Mohan 5 units @ Rs 400. Total is:
Sales returns: Shyam 5 units @ Rs 500; Gopal 4 units @ Rs 450. Total is:

Sales to P Rs 12,000 less 5%; Q Rs 9,000; R Rs 6,500. Total of sales book is:

A bill of exchange is drawn by the _____ on the _____, with the _____ being the person to whom payment is made:
A promissory note is:
options: An unconditional written promise by the maker to pay a certain sum

questions.question_text: A bill of exchange differs from a promissory note in that a bill is:
options: An order by the drawer to the drawee and needs acceptance
questions.explanation: A promissory note has two parties; a bill has three.

questions.question_text: Days of grace are:
options: Three extra days allowed for payment after the due date
questions.explanation: The due date includes the three days of grace.

questions.question_text: The due date of a 3-month bill drawn on 15 January is:
The due date of a 60-day bill drawn on 10 March is:
questions.explanation: 60 days → 9 May; plus 3 days of grace.

questions.question_text: The bills receivable book is posted by:
options: Debiting Bills Receivable A/c and crediting each drawee/customer
questions.explanation: The total is debited; each party is credited.

questions.question_text: The bills payable book is posted by:
options: Debiting each creditor and crediting Bills Payable A/c with the total

questions.question_text: Bills receivable differ from bills payable in that bills receivable are:
options: Assets (accepted by others in our favour), bills payable are liabilities

questions.question_text: When a bill is dishonoured:
options: The drawee fails to pay on the due date, and the drawer debits the drawee again
questions.explanation: Bills Receivable is credited and the drawee is debited.

questions.question_text: Discounting a bill means:
options: Encashing it with the bank before the due date at a discount

questions.question_text: Endorsement of a bill means:
options: Transferring it to a third party by signing the back
questions.explanation: The endorsee gets the right to payment.

questions.question_text: Retirement of a bill means:
options: Payment of the bill by the acceptor before its due date

questions.question_text: A bill of Rs 10,000 discounted with the bank for Rs 9,800. Discount charged is:
options: Rs 200 (Bank Dr 9,800; Discount Dr 200; Bills Receivable Cr 10,000)

questions.question_text: A bill payable of Rs 10,000 honoured on the due date is recorded by:
options: Bills Payable A/c Dr to Cash/Bank A/c

questions.question_text: A bill of Rs 6,000 received from a customer was dishonoured. The entry is:
A cash book is:
options: A book recording all cash receipts and payments
questions.explanation: It records the cash and bank transactions.

questions.question_text: The cash book is both a journal and a ledger because:
options: It is a book of original entry and also serves as the cash account
questions.explanation: It is the only book with this double role.

questions.question_text: The types of cash books include:
options: Single column, double column, three column and petty cash book
questions.explanation: They differ in the number of columns.

questions.question_text: A single column cash book has:
options: One amount column on each side for cash

questions.question_text: A double column cash book has:
options: Two amount columns on each side, e.g., cash and bank (or discount)

questions.question_text: A three column cash book has:
options: Discount, cash and bank columns on each side
questions.explanation: It is the most complete form.

questions.question_text: A contra entry is:
options: An entry affecting both the cash and bank columns of the cash book, e.g., deposit of cash into the bank
questions.explanation: Cash deposited and cash withdrawn from the bank are contra entries.

questions.question_text: Cash deposited in the bank is recorded as:
options: Debit in the bank column and credit in the cash column
Debit in cash and credit in bank

questions.question_text: Cash withdrawn from the bank for office use is recorded as:
options: Debit in the cash column and credit in the bank column

questions.question_text: A credit balance in the bank column indicates:
questions.explanation: The bank has given an overdraft facility.

questions.question_text: The discount column on the debit side of the cash book represents:
questions.explanation: Discount allowed to customers is a loss.

questions.question_text: The discount column on the credit side represents:
questions.explanation: Discount received from suppliers is a gain.

questions.question_text: The totals of the discount columns are posted to:
options: Debit of Discount Allowed A/c and credit of Discount Received A/c
questions.explanation: Individually they are posted to parties' accounts.

questions.question_text: Discount columns are not balanced because:
options: They are memorandum columns, only totalled
questions.explanation: The totals are posted to nominal accounts.

questions.question_text: A dishonoured cheque is recorded in the cash book on the:
options: Debit side of the bank column
Credit side of the bank column

questions.question_text: A cheque issued to a creditor is recorded on the:
options: Debit side of the bank column
Credit side of the bank column

questions.question_text: Single column cash book: opening 5,000; sales 10,000; purchases 6,000; rent 1,000; drawings 2,000. Closing cash is:
Double column cash book: cash 3,000, bank 12,000; deposits 2,000; supplier paid by cheque 5,000; cash sale 4,000. Closing cash and bank:
Cash and discount: received 1,950 (disc 50); paid 2,900 (disc 100); closing balance 5,000. The opening balance was:
In a three column cash book, the balance of the cash column cannot be:
questions.explanation: Cash paid cannot exceed cash available.

questions.question_text: Cash 10,000; Bank 30,000; cheque from X 5,000 (disc 100); rent 2,000 paid in cash; cash deposited 3,000; cheque to Y 8,000 (disc 200). Closing bank balance is:
Cash sales 7,000; wages 1,500 paid in cash; bank withdrawal 2,000 for personal use; cheque from Z 4,900 (disc 100). The net change in the bank column is:

Closing bank balance 27,500; receipts (excluding opening) 14,000; payments 6,500. Opening balance was:
The petty cash book is maintained by:
options: The petty cashier to record small expenses
questions.explanation: It handles minor payments like postage.

questions.question_text: The imprest system is where:
options: A fixed sum is given to the petty cashier and the amount spent is reimbursed periodically
questions.explanation: The advance is restored to the original amount.

questions.question_text: An advantage of the imprest system is:
options: Better control over petty cash and small expenses
questions.explanation: The head cashier knows the exact spending.

questions.question_text: An analytical petty cash book:
options: Classifies expenses under separate columns, e.g., postage, stationery

questions.question_text: Imprest 2,000; postage 300; stationery 400; conveyance 250; sundries 150. The reimbursement is:
In an analytical petty cash book, the sum of the analysis columns equals:
Under the imprest system, the amount reimbursed equals:
options: The total amount spent during the period

questions.question_text: Petty cash totals are posted to the ledger by:
options: Debiting the expense accounts with the column totals

questions.question_text: A cash book differs from a petty cash book in that a petty cash book records:
options: Small routine expenses, while the cash book records all cash transactions
questions.explanation: It is maintained by a petty cashier.

questions.question_text: A cash book differs from a cash account in that the cash book is:
options: A book of original entry, and a cash account is part of the ledger
questions.explanation: The cash book serves as both.

questions.question_text: While balancing the cash book:
options: Total both sides, find the difference, and enter the balance on the smaller side as c/d
questions.explanation: Then bring it down as b/d.

questions.question_text: Which is recorded in the journal proper?
options: Opening, closing, adjusting and rectification entries

questions.question_text: Credit sale of an old asset worth Rs 5,000 is journalised as:
Outstanding wages Rs 3,000 are journalised as:
options: Wages A/c Dr to Outstanding Wages A/c

questions.question_text: Rectification of goods taken by the proprietor Rs 2,000 (unrecorded):
options: Drawings A/c Dr to Purchases A/c

questions.question_text: Writing off bad debt Rs 700:
options: Bad Debts A/c Dr to Debtor

questions.question_text: Closing entry for purchases Rs 80,000:
options: Purchases A/c Dr to Trading A/c
Trading A/c Dr to Purchases A/c
questions.explanation: The expense is closed by crediting it.

questions.question_text: Under GST, special-purpose records include:
options: Input tax credit and output tax details in purchases and sales books
questions.explanation: GST requires separate tracking of tax.

questions.question_text: The sales book records _____ and is posted to _____:
options: Credit sales of goods; debit of customers and credit of Sales A/c
questions.explanation: Nature, entry and posting differ among books.

questions.question_text: Subsidiary books help prepare the trial balance by:
options: Providing totals that are posted to the ledger accounts

questions.question_text: Large firms prefer subsidiary books because they:
questions.explanation: Work can be divided among clerks.

questions.question_text: If the sales book total is posted wrongly:
options: The trial balance will not agree (or the error is found when totals are checked)

questions.question_text: Purchases book: Kiran Rs 12,000 less 10%; Lal Rs 9,000. Total is:
Sales book: Anil Rs 18,000 less 5%; Bimal Rs 7,500. Total is:
Returns inward: Anil Rs 1,800; Bimal Rs 500. Total is:

The purchases book total is posted to the:
options: Debit of Purchases A/c, and each supplier is credited individually

questions.question_text: Cash 8,000; bank 25,000; cheque from P 9,800 (discount 200); paid Q Rs 4,900 cash (discount 100); deposited cash 3,000; rent by cheque 2,000. Closing cash and bank:
The sales book differs from the sales account in that the sales book is:
options: A book of original entry for credit sales, and the sales account is a ledger account
questions.explanation: The total is posted to the sales account.

questions.question_text: The cash book is considered more important than other subsidiary books because it:
options: Records cash and bank transactions and serves as both journal and ledger
questions.explanation: It shows the cash and bank position.
